title: Utilization (prototype)
description: Fleet-wide CPU, memory and GPU use, with a table of nodes to inspect; the Node row below shows one node. Three hub queries per load, and three more when the Node row is open.

list.name: bin
list.label: Bin
list.description: At least 2 minutes: node agent samples arrive about every 60.7 s, so a 1-minute bin can miss one.

list.name: node
list.label: Node
list.description: Set by clicking a node in Nodes to inspect, or typed.

panels.title: GPUs held and busy per cluster
panels.description: Per ${bin}, per CoreWeave cluster: GPUs held are the GPUs that reported inventory in the bin (a GPU present for part of the bin counts fully); GPUs busy are the sum of each GPU's mean SM-active ratio over its samples in the bin. The query is in the Nodes to inspect panel, which this panel reuses.

panels.title: Nodes to inspect
panels.description: One row per GPU node in the range: its GPU type; GPUs held (GPUs that reported inventory in a bin, a GPU present for part of a bin counting fully) and GPUs busy and tensor-active (sums of each GPU's mean ratio in a bin), each averaged over the range's bins; and idle GPUs (held minus busy). Sorted by idle GPUs. Rack, slot, node pool, instance type and IB fabric come from Kubernetes node labels (/k8s/nodes, which needs the CoreWeave read token; empty without it). Click a node to open it in the Node row below. This panel's finelog query also feeds the GPU panel.

params.value: WITH gpu AS ( SELECT cluster, node_name,  date_bin(INTERVAL ${bin:sqlstring}, to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms), TIMESTAMP '1970-01-01 00:00:00') AS bin,  json_get(attributes_json, 'gpu_uuid') AS gpu_uuid,  max(CASE WHEN name = 'hardware_inventory' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS held,  max(CASE WHEN name = 'hardware_inventory' THEN json_get(attributes_json, 'gpu_model') END) AS gpu_model,  avg(CASE WHEN name = 'gpu_sm_active_ratio' THEN value END) AS sm_active,  avg(CASE WHEN name = 'gpu_tensor_active_ratio' THEN value END) AS tensor_active FROM "telemetry_v1.node_agent" WHERE service = 'iris-node-agent' AND name IN ('hardware_inventory', 'gpu_sm_active_ratio', 'gpu_tensor_active_ratio') AND json_get(attributes_json, 'gpu_uuid') IS NOT NULL AND cluster IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4 HAVING date_bin(INTERVAL ${bin:sqlstring}, to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms), TIMESTAMP '1970-01-01 00:00:00') + INTERVAL ${bin:sqlstring} <= {{to}}) SELECT cluster, node_name, bin, sum(held) AS gpus_held, sum(COALESCE(sm_active, 0)) AS gpus_busy,  sum(COALESCE(tensor_active, 0)) AS gpus_tensor_active, max(gpu_model) AS gpu_model FROM gpu GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 ORDER BY 3, 1, 2

panels.title: CPU cores in use
panels.description:
CPU cores in use per ${bin} per cluster: each running attempt's mean CPU from iris.task in the bin, summed. This panel's query also feeds the memory panel.

SQL ({{from}} and {{to}} are the dashboard time range; the bridge fills them in.):

```sql
SELECT cluster, bin, sum(cpu_cores) AS cpu_cores, sum(memory_bytes) AS memory_bytes FROM ( SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(cluster, ''), 'marin') AS cluster,  date_bin(INTERVAL ${bin:sqlstring}, ts, TIMESTAMP '1970-01-01 00:00:00') AS bin, task_id, attempt_id,  avg(cpu_millicores) / 1000.0 AS cpu_cores, avg(memory_mb) * 1048576 AS memory_bytes FROM "iris.task" WHERE ts >= {{from}} AND ts < {{to}} GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4 HAVING date_bin(INTERVAL ${bin:sqlstring}, ts, TIMESTAMP '1970-01-01 00:00:00') + INTERVAL ${bin:sqlstring} <= {{to}}) WHERE cluster IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
```

panels.title: Memory in use
panels.description: Memory in use per ${bin} per cluster, summed over running attempts. Reuses the CPU panel's query.

panels.title: TPU VMs held
panels.description:
TPU VMs that reported inventory per ${bin}, per cluster and TPU type: distinct node_name, which on a TPU VM is its GCE instance name, one per worker of a multi-host slice. TPUs have no use signal; chips held is VMs times chips per VM of the type.

SQL ({{from}} and {{to}} are the dashboard time range; the bridge fills them in.):

```sql
SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(cluster, ''), 'marin') AS cluster, date_bin(INTERVAL ${bin:sqlstring}, to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms), TIMESTAMP '1970-01-01 00:00:00') AS bin, json_get(attributes_json, 'tpu_type') AS tpu_type, count(DISTINCT node_name) AS tpu_vms_held FROM "telemetry_v1.node_agent" WHERE service = 'iris-node-agent' AND name = 'hardware_inventory' AND json_get(attributes_json, 'device_kind') = 'tpu' AND COALESCE(NULLIF(cluster, ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 HAVING date_bin(INTERVAL ${bin:sqlstring}, to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms), TIMESTAMP '1970-01-01 00:00:00') + INTERVAL ${bin:sqlstring} <= {{to}} ORDER BY 1, 2, 3
```

options.content: Use by category needs the job tag column, which the controller does not write yet. Splitting by category joins every attempt to its job, the costly lookback, so it will likely come from a precomputed table rather than a live query.

panels.title: Jobs on the node
panels.description:
One line per job: 1 while an attempt of the job runs on ${node}, 0 otherwise, stacked so two jobs at once read 2. The table below lists the attempts. Attempts whose newest row is older than 1 day before the range start are missed. This panel's query also feeds the table.

SQL ({{from}} and {{to}} are the dashboard time range; the bridge fills them in.):

```sql
WITH attempt AS ( SELECT cluster, root_job_id, root_submitted_at_ms, job_id, submitted_at_ms, task_id, attempt_id, attempt_uid, state, started_at, finished_at FROM (  SELECT cluster, root_job_id, root_submitted_at_ms, job_id, submitted_at_ms, task_id, attempt_id, attempt_uid, state, started_at, finished_at,   row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY attempt_uid ORDER BY ts DESC, seq DESC) AS rn  FROM "iris.controller_db__task_attempts"  WHERE (node_name = ${node:sqlstring} OR worker_id = ${node:sqlstring})   AND ts >= {{from}} - INTERVAL '1 day' AND ts < {{to}} ) WHERE rn = 1 AND started_at IS NOT NULL AND started_at < {{to}}   AND COALESCE(finished_at, {{to}}) > {{from}}), job AS ( SELECT cluster, root_job_id, root_submitted_at_ms, job_id, submitted_at_ms, user_id, name FROM (  SELECT cluster, root_job_id, root_submitted_at_ms, job_id, submitted_at_ms, user_id, name,   row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY cluster, root_job_id, root_submitted_at_ms, job_id, submitted_at_ms ORDER BY ts DESC, seq DESC) AS rn  FROM "iris.controller_db__jobs"  WHERE ts >= {{from}} - INTERVAL '1 day' AND ts < {{to}}   AND root_job_id IN (SELECT root_job_id FROM attempt) ) WHERE rn = 1), request AS ( SELECT cluster, root_job_id, root_submitted_at_ms, job_id, submitted_at_ms, res_cpu_millicores, res_memory_bytes, accelerator_kind, accelerator_type,  accelerators_per_task FROM (  SELECT cluster, root_job_id, root_submitted_at_ms, job_id, submitted_at_ms, res_cpu_millicores, res_memory_bytes, accelerator_kind, accelerator_type,   accelerators_per_task,   row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY cluster, root_job_id, root_submitted_at_ms, job_id, submitted_at_ms ORDER BY ts DESC, seq DESC) AS rn  FROM "iris.controller_db__job_config"  WHERE ts >= {{from}} - INTERVAL '1 day' AND ts < {{to}}   AND root_job_id IN (SELECT root_job_id FROM attempt) ) WHERE rn = 1), grid AS ( SELECT unnest(generate_series(date_bin(INTERVAL '1 minute', {{from}}, TIMESTAMP '1970-01-01 00:00:00'),  {{to}}, INTERVAL '1 minute')) AS minute) SELECT g.minute, a.attempt_uid, a.task_id, a.attempt_id, a.job_id, j.user_id, j.name AS job_name, a.state,  a.started_at, a.finished_at, r.res_cpu_millicores / 1000.0 AS cpu_request,  r.res_memory_bytes AS memory_request_bytes, r.accelerator_kind, r.accelerator_type,  r.accelerators_per_task, CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR) AS category,  CASE WHEN a.started_at < g.minute + INTERVAL '1 minute'   AND COALESCE(a.finished_at, {{to}}) > g.minute THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS active FROM attempt a LEFT JOIN job j USING (cluster, root_job_id, root_submitted_at_ms, job_id, submitted_at_ms) LEFT JOIN request r USING (cluster, root_job_id, root_submitted_at_ms, job_id, submitted_at_ms) CROSS JOIN grid g WHERE g.minute < {{to}} ORDER BY g.minute, a.job_id, a.attempt_uid
```

panels.title: GPU SM-active per GPU
panels.description:
Per-minute SM-active ratio of each GPU on ${node} (CoreWeave nodes only). This panel's query also feeds the tensor-active, host CPU and host memory panels.

SQL ({{from}} and {{to}} are the dashboard time range; the bridge fills them in.):

```sql
SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '1 minute', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms), TIMESTAMP '1970-01-01 00:00:00') AS minute, name, json_get(attributes_json, 'gpu_index') AS gpu_index, avg(value) AS value FROM "telemetry_v1.node_agent" WHERE service = 'iris-node-agent' AND node_name = ${node:sqlstring} AND name IN ('gpu_sm_active_ratio', 'gpu_tensor_active_ratio', 'gpu_power_watts', 'node_cpu_utilization_percent', 'node_memory_used_bytes', 'node_memory_total_bytes') AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 ORDER BY 1, 2, 3
```

params.value: SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '1 minute', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms), TIMESTAMP '1970-01-01 00:00:00') AS minute, name, json_get(attributes_json, 'gpu_index') AS gpu_index, avg(value) AS value FROM "telemetry_v1.node_agent" WHERE service = 'iris-node-agent' AND node_name = ${node:sqlstring} AND name IN ('gpu_sm_active_ratio', 'gpu_tensor_active_ratio', 'gpu_power_watts', 'node_cpu_utilization_percent', 'node_memory_used_bytes', 'node_memory_total_bytes') AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 ORDER BY 1, 2, 3

panels.title: Host CPU
panels.description: Per-minute host CPU utilization of ${node}. The node agent writes host rows only while it can read the node's host source (node-exporter on CoreWeave), so a node without one shows no data. Reuses the SM-active panel's query.

panels.title: CPU cores per attempt
panels.description:
Per-minute CPU cores each attempt on ${node} used, from iris.task. This panel's query also feeds the memory panel.

SQL ({{from}} and {{to}} are the dashboard time range; the bridge fills them in.):

```sql
WITH attempt AS ( SELECT cluster, task_id, attempt_id, started_at, finished_at FROM (  SELECT cluster, task_id, attempt_id, attempt_uid, started_at, finished_at,   row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY attempt_uid ORDER BY ts DESC, seq DESC) AS rn  FROM "iris.controller_db__task_attempts"  WHERE (node_name = ${node:sqlstring} OR worker_id = ${node:sqlstring})   AND ts >= {{from}} - INTERVAL '1 day' AND ts < {{to}} ) WHERE rn = 1 AND started_at IS NOT NULL AND started_at < {{to}}   AND COALESCE(finished_at, {{to}}) > {{from}}) SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '1 minute', t.ts, TIMESTAMP '1970-01-01 00:00:00') AS minute,  t.task_id || ':' || CAST(t.attempt_id AS VARCHAR) AS attempt,  avg(t.cpu_millicores) / 1000.0 AS cpu_cores, avg(t.memory_mb) * 1048576 AS memory_bytes FROM "iris.task" t JOIN attempt a  ON COALESCE(NULLIF(t.cluster, ''), 'marin') = a.cluster  AND t.task_id = a.task_id AND t.attempt_id = a.attempt_id  AND t.ts >= a.started_at AND t.ts <= COALESCE(a.finished_at, {{to}}) WHERE t.ts >= {{from}} AND t.ts < {{to}}  AND t.task_id IN (SELECT task_id FROM attempt) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
```
